s: A Guinness-certified record: continuously trading books from the same Chiado address since 1773.
w: Founded in 1732 by Pedro Faure and rebuilt on Rua Garrett after the 1755 earthquake flattened its first premises, Bertrand has sold books from this address for two and a half centuries -- long enough that Guinness World Records certified it, in 2011, as the oldest operating bookshop on Earth. Vaulted rooms run back through the building like a spine, ending in a small courtyard café.
_facts: Founded 1732 by Pedro Faure; moved to this address in 1773
Certified by Guinness World Records in 2011 as the world's oldest bookshop still in operation
Vaulted 18th-century interior with a rear courtyard café

n: Officina Profumo-Farmaceutica di Santa Maria Novella
q: Officina Profumo Farmaceutica Santa Maria Novella Florence
s: Dominican friars started distilling remedies here in 1221; the frescoed sales hall still sells what they made.
w: Dominican friars at Santa Maria Novella were growing medicinal herbs by 1221, and by 1612 the monastery's apothecary was selling rosewater and balms to the public under Medici grand-ducal charter -- arguably the oldest pharmacy in continuous operation anywhere. Its green-and-gold former sacristy, frescoed ceiling intact, now serves as the retail hall, trading in soaps, potpourri and liqueurs distilled a few rooms away.
_facts: Dominican friars cultivated medicinal herbs on the site from 1221
Opened to the public as a pharmacy in 1612 under Medici charter
Frescoed former sacristy rooms serve as the sales hall

q: Libreria Acqua Alta Venice bookshop gondola
s: Flood-proofed shelving, Venetian-style: bathtubs, a gondola, and a rear staircase built from unsold paperbacks.
w: When acqua alta rises through Castello's calli, most shopkeepers roll out barriers; this shop just built its shelving from things that already float. Paperbacks fill a full-size gondola, a rusting canoe and several bathtubs, and a back courtyard staircase is built entirely from waterlogged stock that never sold, fused into steps by weather and time.
_facts: Owned by Luigi Frizzo, opened in the early 2000s specifically to withstand seasonal flooding
Stock is stored in a gondola, a canoe, and bathtubs
A rear-courtyard staircase is built from decades of flood-damaged unsold books

s: George Whitman opened it as Le Mistral in 1951, across the Seine from Notre-Dame, and let writers sleep among the stacks.
w: Whitman named his shop after Sylvia Beach's storied Left Bank bookstore only in 1964, on Shakespeare's 400th birthday -- two decades after Beach's original had shut under Nazi occupation. His version, opened in 1951 at this address, kept faith with the same idea: more than 30,000 'tumbleweeds,' aspiring writers and drifters, have slept among its shelves in exchange for shop work.
_facts: Opened 1951 by George Whitman as 'Le Mistral'; renamed Shakespeare and Company in 1964
Distinct from Sylvia Beach's original 1919-1941 shop of the same name
Over 30,000 'tumbleweeds' have slept in the shop in exchange for work

s: A working dairy shop tiled floor to ceiling in hand-painted Villeroy & Boch majolica, certified since 1998 as the world's most beautiful.
w: Paul Pfund opened his dairy in 1880 to sell clean milk to a city rattled by adulterated supplies; by 1891 the shop had been rebuilt in Neo-Renaissance tile from Villeroy & Boch -- cherubs, garlands and dairy cows tiled floor to ceiling. Guinness certified it in 1998 as the world's most beautiful dairy shop. Cheese, milk products and its own cosmetics line are still sold under the tile.
_facts: Founded 1880; current tiled building dates to 1891
Tilework by Villeroy & Boch in Neo-Renaissance majolica style
Guinness World Records-listed since 1998 as the World's Most Beautiful Dairy Shop

s: A full city block of new and used stock, colour-coded by room, that calls itself the world's largest independent bookstore.
w: Michael Powell brought his father's Chicago bookstore idea to Portland in 1971, and it grew into a full city block of nine colour-coded rooms spanning roughly 68,000 square feet of new and secondhand stock shelved together by subject. Staff still hand-write the shelf-talker recommendation cards. Maps are handed out at the door, because without one the Rose Room and the Gold Room look identical.
_facts: Opened 1971 in Portland by Michael Powell
Occupies a full city block; roughly 68,000 sq ft across nine colour-coded rooms
New and used books are shelved together by subject

a: Freeport A'Famosa Outlet, Simpang Ampat, Alor Gajah
s: A grounded 1981 Boeing 747, gutted and refitted as a Coach handbag store and café, parked permanently at an outlet mall.
w: Coach spent from April 2021 to May 2023 converting a retired 1981 Boeing 747-230B into a two-level retail concept store and café at this outlet mall outside Malacca -- cockpit, fuselage and all, repainted and refitted rather than demolished. It relaunched with a redesigned cabin, cockpit and flooring in mid-2025.
_facts: Converted from a 1981 Boeing 747-230B; conversion ran April 2021 to May 2023
Marketed as the world's first retail concept store inside a converted 747
Redesigned/relaunched with new interior finishes in mid-2025

s: Five floors of kinetic sculpture built in-house by an eyewear brand's own robotics lab, selling sunglasses almost as an afterthought.
w: Gentle Monster's flagship treats retail as gallery: reed-like kinetic sculptures sway on motors through the ground floor, and the brand's in-house robotics lab has installed 'The Probe,' a six-legged robotic creature, on an upper level. The building also houses Tamburins (cosmetics) and Nudake (dessert), so a single visit moves through perfume counters, a pastry bar and an art installation before it reaches a rack of sunglasses.
_facts: Gentle Monster's Seoul flagship 'Haus' concept space
Features in-house-built kinetic sculptures and 'The Probe' robot
Shares the building with sister brands Tamburins and Nudake

s: A 14-storey multi-brand tower in Seongsu, opened 2025, that treats shopping as a single continuous art installation.
w: Gentle Monster's second Seoul 'Haus' opened in the industrial-turned-hip Seongsu district as a 14-storey retail tower, each floor handed to a different brand experience rather than a fixed department layout. Reviewers describe it as less a store than a building-sized exhibition you're allowed to buy things inside.
_facts: Opened 2025 in Seongsu-dong
A 14-storey building, Gentle Monster's largest concept space to date
Multi-brand format spanning fashion, cosmetics and dessert concepts

a: Road No. 12, Kaushik Society, Banjara Hills
s: A 10,000-square-foot working chocolate factory in Banjara Hills where the roasting, tempering and moulding happen in view of the counter.
w: Manam's Karkhana ('workshop') is a bean-to-bar operation you can watch in motion -- cocoa roasted, ground and tempered in an open factory floor that shares its footprint with a retail counter and café. It's one of the few Indian craft-chocolate producers running the entire process, sourcing to sale, under a single roof rather than importing couverture.
_facts: 10,000 sq ft combined factory, retail store and café
Runs the full bean-to-bar process on site
Offers ticketed factory tours in addition to retail sales

s: A former locksmith's courtyard workshop, now a bare-concrete concept store selling clothes, books and coffee under gallery lighting.
w: Set back from Oranienstrasse through a Kreuzberg courtyard, Voo occupies what used to be a locksmith's workshop -- 300 square metres of exposed concrete now hung with premium fashion, art books and the odd curated object, lit like a gallery rather than a shop floor. It doubles as a small venue: readings, listening sessions and exhibitions run alongside the racks.
_facts: Occupies a former locksmith's workshop in a courtyard off Oranienstraße
Roughly 300 sq m of retail space with an in-house café
Regularly hosts readings, exhibitions and music events

q: Printemps New York One Wall Street
s: A 160-year-old Parisian department store's first US outpost, entered through a 1931 mosaic hall thirty feet tall.
w: Printemps' first American store, opened March 2025, took over two floors of the Art Deco former Irving Trust headquarters at One Wall Street -- 55,000 square feet designed to feel like a Parisian apartment rather than a sales floor. One entrance leads straight into the building's landmarked Red Room: a 30-foot mosaic of red and gold tile made by muralist Hildreth Meière in 1931, left largely as it was for bank customers a century ago.
_facts: Opened March 21, 2025 -- Printemps' first US location
Occupies 55,000 sq ft of the former Irving Trust / One Wall Street building
Incorporates the landmarked 1931 Hildreth Meière 'Red Room' mosaic hall
